title: LoRAScan: Detecting Backdoor Prompts in Low-Rank Adapters for Large Language Models via Down-Projection Activation Spikes
abstract: arXiv:2608.06795v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables efficient specialization and distribution of large language models through compact adapters. However, untrusted adapters introduce a supply-chain threat: a backdoored adapter can cause a model to generate harmful content, malicious code, political propaganda, or covert advertisements when an input contains a hidden trigger. Adapter-agnostic defenses merge the adapter with the base model, which dilutes backdoor signals and reduces detection performance. Existing adapter-aware methods do not address how to safely use a potentially backdoored adapter. Instead, they either train a defensive adapter to repair a backdoored base model, addressing the inverse problem rather than securing the adapter itself, or rely on a classifier that flags the entire adapter as suspicious and requires separate mitigation. These methods overlook the distinct latent-space signatures produced by trigger-bearing inputs

translated_title: LoRAScan：通过下投影激活尖峰检测大语言模型低秩适配器中的后门提示
translated_abstract: 低秩适配（LoRA）通过紧凑的适配器实现了大语言模型的高效专门化与分发。然而，不可信的适配器会带来供应链威胁：当输入包含隐藏触发器时，带有后门的适配器可能导致模型生成有害内容、恶意代码、政治宣传或隐蔽广告。与适配器无关的防御方法会将适配器与基础模型合并，这会稀释后门信号并降低检测性能。现有的适配器感知方法并未解决如何安全地使用可能带有后门的适配器：它们要么训练一个防御性适配器来修复带有后门的基础模型（解决的是相反的问题，而非保护适配器本身），要么依赖一个将整个适配器标记为可疑的分类器，且需要单独的缓解措施。这些方法都忽略了携带触发器的输入在潜空间中产生的独特特征。
tldr: 该论文提出LoRAScan方法，利用携带触发器的输入在下投影层产生的激活尖峰这一独特潜空间特征，来检测大语言模型LoRA适配器中的后门提示。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes LoRAScan, a method that detects backdoor prompts in LoRA adapters for LLMs by leveraging the distinct activation spikes in down-projection layers produced by trigger-bearing inputs.
